newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea hands back North Korean remains.
newsitem.headline: South Korea hands back North Korean remains.

text.p: The remains of 24 North Koreans shot dead after coming ashore from a submarine that infiltrated into South Korea in September were handed back across the border on Monday, state radio reported.
South Korea's defence ministry earlier said cremated remains would be handed back in boxes, correcting initial reports saying bodies would be delivered in coffins.

The ashes were returned through the border village of Panmunjom under an agreement reached between the U.S.-led United Nations Command and North Korean representatives in a border meeting on Monday. The U.N. command supervises a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Seoul swiftly agreed to send home the remains after Pyongyang apologised on Sunday for the submarine incursion in an uprecedented statement of contrition towards the South.

Out of 26 North Koreans that landed from the vessel, 11 were found shot dead -- apparently in a mass suicide -- and 13 were killed by Southern forces during a massive manhunt. One was captured alive and one is still at large.
